questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always wanted to live in Iceland as my mother is from Iceland. It was important that the University had courses that made sense for me and that were related to my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright but i think it was a little bit confusing at some points and there were things that i missed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A bit of information at the service desk but not much in the beginning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student apartments or shared spaces i lived in a shared dorm space with my own bathroom in my room and i was very happy with that.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: shared kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure as there are multiple different student housing options and they are all different in some ways

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember everything at this point but i had to go to the service desk to register on the day i arrived.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Service desk. my first few days in iceland were introduction days for excahnge students and we were provided with a program via a link from the university so we could see where to be. there were some changes and i remember being a bit confused much of the time during my first days but it was also really fun.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: pretty successful. I registered for the courses i was most interested in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To talk to other exchange students if you are confused about something. it helps to know you are not alone if they do not know something either and if they do they can help you find out what you need to do.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I'm not entirely sure. I think my courses were mostly BA level but i had some courses where there were a mix of BA and MA students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different overall. One major difference was the use of multiple choice tests which i had to do many of throughout the semester and i don't remember having done any of those while studying at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Icelandic Culture
British and European Cultural History
British Literature from Early Middle Ages to 1603
All that glitters is not gold: gender, equality and sustainability in Iceland
Apocalypse Descending: AIDS, The Cold War and American Culture in 'Angels in America'

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking one of the courses on Icelandic Culture if you are interested in learning about the country and these course are specifically for international students as well as for exchange students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It is a bit difficult to remember everything from my exchange but Iceland is very expensive and i had planned to keep my shopping of clothes to an absolute minimum but there were times where i needed something and many other exchange students had underestimated how cold it can be and needed to buy winter jackets and wool underlayers which is needed when it is cold and windy. i also needed to buy a router from the bookstore because i live on campus and the internet is not good in the student housing. There was a student festical that was pretty expensive that i chose to go to. i also went to the swimming pools a lot which is part of icelandic culture which cost money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I already knew that Iceland was very expensive but i just want to emphasize how expensive it is to stay in Iceland for so long and groceries were really expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Student festival, karaoke events, pub quiz

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the karaoke events and pub quiz events

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the pool it is a huge part of Icelandic culture. go hiking. rent a car and trval around outside of reykjavik.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, i am half Icelandic

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The swimming pool culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
get a 10 or 20 use card for the swimming pools in reykjavik. they can be used in all pools withing the reykjavik municipality and it is absolutely amazing. When you have used them all you can get your cards refilled. 
On campus there is a really nice bar that is open every day. you can get food and coffee and etc and study there during the day but this is also where many of the events such as karaoke and pub quiz will take place and you will probably spend a lot of time here with other exchange students.
Bring merino wool underlayers for the winter.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: That it is best to live on campus or as close to campus as possible or in the area. There are busses but they do not go very late and it can take a long time with the bus if you live outside of reykjavik.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed my courses adn other than that it was rewarding to socialize with people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me it was to be more independent and try figuring out things although they were different than at my home university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
